title: fix(plugin-sharing): warn once per boot when a hierarchy scope falls back to owner-only
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao6bxiPKCvVuzoFTExumbxoz)_
Fixes #35172
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：运维人员在不经命令行启动的运行时里，第一次有人用到上下级可见范围而企业版组件没装时，日志里会出现一条警告，说明这些范围只按本人记录生效；终端用户无感。
- 为什么做：属于权限可见性排查这条线，替自托管运行时的运维人员解决「为什么每个人只看得到自己的记录」查不到原因的问题。
- 出错会怎样：最坏是这条警告不出现或多出现几次，访问结果本身不变；可以直接撤回。
- 要你做什么：无

## What changes

`SharingService.resolveOwnerScopeIds` (plugin-sharing) fails closed to owner-only when a hierarchy scope (`own_and_reports`, `unit`, `unit_and_below`) is asked for and no `hierarchy-scope-resolver` service is registered. That branch used to log nothing, so only `os serve` (the CLI line added by #35168) ever said so.

- The first time that fallback is taken, the service logs one `warn` (`HIERARCHY_RESOLVER_ABSENT_NOTICE`), with meta `{ capability: 'hierarchy-security', provider, scope }`. The provider is read from `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS['hierarchy-security'].package`, so it is the same `@objectstack/security-enterprise` string `os validate` / `os verify` / `os serve` print. The prefix and level match the no-org warning just below it (`[sharing] hierarchy scope NOT widened: ...`, `warn`). Per AGENTS.md "Degradation log levels", this is a functional degradation, so `warn` is the right level.
- **Once per boot.** The latch is a boolean on the service instance. The plugin builds exactly one `SharingService`, in its `kernel:ready` hook (`sharing-plugin.ts`), so one instance means one boot. The callers (read filter, write gates, share management, middleware) run per request. The condition belongs to the composition, not to a caller or an object, so a finer key would only repeat the line. The latch is claimed before the log, inside a `try`, so a throwing logger cannot fail a gate or throw once per request.
- **Only when the fallback is taken.** `own`, `org` and an unset scope return before the resolver lookup, so an app that never uses a hierarchy scope logs nothing. A registered resolver also logs nothing.
- **The CLI stops claiming silence for this token** (patch round 1, claim amendment 7033136082). `enterpriseAbsenceConsequence` (`packages/cli/src/utils/capability-preflight.ts`) used to end every enterprise-token sentence with "and no log line says so". A new table, `ENTERPRISE_ABSENCE_RUNTIME_NOTICE`, maps a token to the opening words of the warning its runtime logs. For `hierarchy-security`, the sentence now says the runtime logs one warning (`[sharing] hierarchy scope NOT widened ...`) the first time it falls back. Any token without a row keeps the old clause. I made it a separate table, not a clause folded into `ENTERPRISE_ABSENCE_CONSEQUENCE`, for two reasons. First, the consequence is what the metadata does and the notice is what the runtime says, and a token can have either without the other. Second, the exported table's type stays unchanged.
- **Logging only.** The latch records no verdict: the resolver is still looked up on every call, and the returned ids are unchanged (`[me]`). `check:startup-registry-verdict` is green on this tree.

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in `src/sharing-service.test.ts` (the shared harness file). It has six cases:

- the notice names the capability, the registry provider and the owner-only consequence;
- a resolver-less hierarchy scope warns once across two calls (`unit_and_below`, then `own_and_reports`) plus a public `canManageShares` gate, and every call answers `['bob']`;
- a fresh instance, standing for a new boot, warns again;
- CONTROL: `undefined` / `own` / `org` produce no `warn` at all;
- CONTROL: a registered resolver produces no notice and returns its own ids;
- a throwing logger leaves the answer intact and is called only once.

The plugin-side notice pin also asserts the prefix the CLI quotes.

`packages/cli/test/capability-preflight.test.ts` gains three pins:

- every runtime-notice row keys an enterprise-edition registry token;
- `hierarchy-security` no longer contains "no log line says so" and names the `[sharing] hierarchy scope NOT widened` prefix;
- CONTROL: a generic token still says "no log line says so".

## Acceptance notes

- The round-1 finding (the CLI sentence claiming "no log line says so") is fixed in this PR under the claim amendment.
- Round 2 (claim amendment 7035179372, head `9c805c664c`), comment only: the comment on the unmounted-known-tokens block in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` no longer says the owner-only fallback happens "without a word". It now says the runtime logs it once at the first fallback, and that `os serve` says it at start-up, before any request. Readings on that file: eslint `--no-inline-config` exit 0; check:doc-authoring, check:issue-citations, check:nul-bytes, check:closed-ceremony-text and check-drift-comment all exit 0.
